listening-text-1.transcript:
M: Thanks for the wonderful meal, Mom, I think I’d better go back to my office. I’ve got a report to write.
W: Okay, bye, Luke. Drive with care.

listening-text-7.transcript:
M: Kate, what are you writing?
W: A letter to my sister.
M: Why not send an email to her? It’s faster.
W: Well, I love email for the convenience, but I tend to write letters for pleasure, especially for holiday greetings.
M: You’re right. I prefer handwritten birthday cards too.
W: And I love getting letters too. Hearing a letter drop through the mailbox is much more exciting than getting an email, even though it’s usually a bill or advertisement in my case.
M: Oh, that reminds me, I haven’t checked my mailbox for ages.
listening-text-7.translationZh:
男：凯特，你在写什么？
女：给我妹妹写信。
男：为什么不给她发邮件呢？那样更快。
女：嗯，我喜欢邮件的方便，但我写信往往是图个乐趣，尤其是节日问候。
男：你说得对。我也更喜欢手写的生日卡片。
女：我也喜欢收信。听到信落进信箱的声音，比收到邮件让人兴奋得多，虽然我收到的通常是账单或广告。
男：哦，这倒提醒我了，我好久没查看信箱了。
listening-text-7.summaryZh: 凯特给妹妹写信，说邮件方便，但写信是图乐趣；男士被提醒自己好久没查信箱。

listening-text-8.transcript:
W: Dear listeners I have with me today Robert jents of the International Dark Sky Association. Robert, Welcome to our program.
M: Thank you. I’m glad to be here.
W: Would you please tell our listeners why you became an Astronomer?
M: When I was a little boy, I loved the night sky. I remember I looked up at the stars in the sky and asked, how many are there? How far away are they? Can we visit them? I became an astronomer because I was amazed by their beauty, but now in most big cities, kids can’t see the stars like I did.
W: So, have you already come up with a solution to this problem?
M: Yeah, Actually, there is a method that is inexpensive and has immediate benefits. If we shine lights down at the ground instead of up into the sky, and use lower brightness levels, we can preserve the beauty of the night sky.
listening-text-8.translationZh:
女：亲爱的听众朋友们，今天来到我身边的是国际暗夜协会的罗伯特。罗伯特，欢迎来到我们的节目。
男：谢谢，很高兴来到这里。
女：能给听众讲讲你为什么成为天文学家吗？
男：我小时候就喜欢夜空。我记得自己抬头望着天上的星星，问：一共有多少颗？它们有多远？我们能去看看它们吗？我成为天文学家，是因为被星星的美震撼了。可是现在在大多数大城市，孩子们已经不能像我当年那样看到星星了。
女：那么，你们想出解决这个问题的办法了吗？
男：是的。其实有一种办法既便宜又能立即见效：如果我们把灯光朝下照向地面，而不是朝上照向天空，并调低亮度，就能保住夜空的美。

listening-text-9.transcript:
M: Elena, who had a great influence on your career?
W: I would say it’s my father. He began to run soccer schools when I was a teenager, so I played soccer with my brother and his friends, but a life in the game was not my plan. So after graduation, I took a job writing technical instructions. It was my first job.
M: What was that like?
W: It paid well, but was not very interesting. So when offered a coaching role, I seized it.
M: Did you have to overcome any challenges to get where you are today?
W: Well, where to start? I enjoyed a successful college life. Then I progressed through The College system to
become an assistant coach to the national team. I’ve encountered a lot of challenges through the ups and downs of being a coach. It’s particularly hard to face the doubts after losing games.
M: What achievement are you most proud of?
W: I’m most proud of helping my team to win all the last seven matches in Italy and Brazil.
M: What are you planning to do next?
W: I’ll take on another challenge, possibly coaching in England.
listening-text-9.translationZh:
男：埃琳娜，谁对你的职业影响最大？
女：我会说是我父亲。我十几岁时他开始办足球学校，所以我和哥哥以及他的朋友们一起踢球，但以足球为生并不在我的计划里。所以毕业后，我找了一份写技术说明书的工作，那是我的第一份工作。
男：那份工作怎么样？
女：收入不错，但不太有意思。所以有人请我当教练时，我就抓住了机会。
男：为了走到今天，你有没有克服什么困难？
女：嗯，从哪儿说起呢？我的大学生活很成功。后来我在大学体系里一步步做起，成为国家队的助理教练。做教练起起落落，我遇到过很多挑战，尤其难的是输球之后要面对各种质疑。
男：你最自豪的成就是什么？
女：我最自豪的是帮助球队在意大利和巴西赢下了最近的全部七场比赛。
男：你接下来有什么打算？
女：我会接受新的挑战，可能去英格兰执教。
listening-text-9.summaryZh: 足球教练埃琳娜讲父亲对她的影响、从技术写作转行当教练的经历、遇到的挑战和下一步打算。

listening-text-10.transcript: Good morning, everyone. I’m Monica from Canada, and I’ll teach you English writing this term. Before we start, I’d like to take a few minutes to let you know something about me. When I was small, I enjoyed spending my summers reading story books instead of playing baseball or taking dance lessons. After I went to school, I took reading time seriously, once I tied one end of a string around a book and the other end around my waist, climbed a tree and sat in the branches reading until dinner time. In college, I thought I might major in journalism or history, but when I took my first literature class, I was deeply attracted to it. The calling to be an English major was in my heart, and I couldn’t imagine spending my study hours without Shakespeare, Chaucer or Lewis by my side. I learned the art of making connections between literature and life and developed a love for writing. After graduation, I taught English in a primary school in Canada for five years. Then I went to Australia and worked as a book editor. Three years ago, I came to China. I’ve been teaching English in middle schools. I love my job, and I’m thankful for the gift of words for the life connection beauty and learning that come from language.
listening-text-10.translationZh: 大家早上好。我是来自加拿大的莫妮卡，这学期教大家英语写作。开始之前，我想花几分钟让大家了解一下我。我小时候喜欢整个夏天读故事书，而不是去打棒球或上舞蹈课。上学以后，我把读书时间看得很重。有一次，我把一根绳子的一头系在书上，另一头系在腰上，爬上树，坐在树枝上一直读到吃晚饭。上大学时，我本以为自己可能会主修新闻或历史，但上了第一堂文学课后，我被文学深深吸引了。做一名英语专业学生成了我内心的召唤，我无法想象学习时身边没有莎士比亚、乔叟或刘易斯。我学会了把文学和生活联系起来，也爱上了写作。毕业后，我在加拿大一所小学教了五年英语。后来我去了澳大利亚，当了图书编辑。三年前我来到中国，一直在中学教英语。我热爱我的工作，感谢文字这份礼物，感谢语言带来的与生活的联结、美和学习。
listening-text-10.summaryZh: 新老师莫妮卡自我介绍：从小爱读书，大学学英语，教过书、做过编辑，现在在中国教英语。

distractors.label: C
